subject: Service locus, telemetry retention, and egress workflow — RFI clarifications
messages:
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@finsecure.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@unihealth.org
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI — service locus / telemetry / egress questions

Karthik / Laura,

Thanks for the quick turn on the RFI. A couple of follow-ups from our security and legal teams so we can finalize the hosting/residency matrix in our procurement packet:

1) Can you define "service locus" as you use it in the RFI? We see references to regional "processing" vs. "control plane" but want a single-sentence commitment we can rely on.

2) Telemetry: what signals do you retain that contain customer identifiers (request IDs, IPs, prompt snippets)? Please include retention windows and where telemetry is stored (EU/US). Our regulator requires proof that EU customer traffic does not leave the EU for storage operations.

3) Egress workflow: are there any operational scenarios (model refresh, kernel updates, failover) that would cause customer data or telemetry to be exported to another region temporarily? If yes, describe controls and notification timelines.

4) We requested audit evidence (SOC2 or equivalent) for historic log retention configurations — can you attach the specific retention matrix you apply per region?

If you can provide a consolidated response and the two requested artifacts (service locus commitment PDF + telemetry retention spreadsheet) by COB Monday 11/9 that would keep us on schedule.

Best,

Sarah Lopez
Senior Security Manager — FinSecure
sarah.lopez@finsecure.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: FinSecure_RFI_questions_v3.pdf (referenced)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: RFI — service locus / telemetry / egress questions (draft responses)

Laura / Marcus — forwarding FinSecure's follow-ups. Draft answers below; please review and flag any compliance/legal concerns before I send back to Sarah. I want to be specific without over-committing.

Quoted original:
> Can you define "service locus" as you use it in the RFI? ...

Draft answers (high level):
- Service locus definition (proposed): "Service locus" = the geographic region(s) where customer request processing and persistent customer data storage occur under the customer's control plane configuration. This excludes model binaries and upstream telemetry used solely for runtime optimization unless explicitly enabled.
- Telemetry retention: we retain operational telemetry (metrics, traces) by default for 30 days in the processing region; request-level debug traces that include prompt text are retained only if a customer enables debug logging and then are retained for 7 days. IPs and connection metadata are redacted by default for EU accounts; full connection metadata retained only in dedicated/private deployments with a contractual clause.
- Egress workflow: normal model updates (weights, parameter deltas) originate from our build artifacts (US/EU mirrors). Customer PII or requests are not included in model weights. We do have a documented failover path where encrypted KV caches may be replicated to a fallback region for continuity; that replication is dual-written only after a configured approval and with customer notified within 2 hours.

Artifacts: I can attach a short service locus commitment PDF and the telemetry retention matrix. Marcus — can you confirm the 30/7 day numbers and the redaction wording here? Also confirm the notice SLA for cross-region replication.

Thanks,
Karthik
Product Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: RFI — service locus / telemetry / egress questions

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Below are our consolidated answers and the two artifacts attached: 20261105-Service-Locus-Commitment.pdf and telemetry-retention-matrix.xlsx.

1) Service locus (short commitment)
"Redwood's service locus for a given customer is the set of cloud regions where that customer's request processing and persistent customer data (prompt text, embeddings, stored artifacts) are processed or stored. For EU-profiled customers (account configured with EU residency), all customer data and request processing will occur within EU regions only, subject to the limited, documented exceptions below. The control plane (deployment orchestration, billing) remains logically centralized but operates over encrypted telemetry and metadata, and does not contain customer prompt contents for EU-residency accounts."

2) Telemetry — what we collect and where it is stored
- Operational metrics & aggregates (latency histograms, token counts): retained 90 days by default in the region of processing; replicated summaries to our analytics service in the us-west-2 analytics cluster for product improvement, but these are aggregated and do not include raw prompts or customer identifiers.
- Traces and debug logs (span-level traces, full request debug): retained 7 days in the processing region when debug logging is enabled; default for most accounts is 30 days aggregated telemetry with prompt text redacted.
- Connection metadata (IP addresses, TLS handshake metadata): for EU-resident accounts we apply IP pseudonymization by default; full IP retention is only enabled under a Dedicated or Private deployment with explicit contractual terms.

3) Egress scenarios and controls
- Model updates: model binaries and training artifacts are distributed via our artifact mirror network. Model updates do not contain customer prompt data. Mirrors exist in EU and US — we will serve model binaries from the EU mirror for EU-resident accounts.
- Failover replication (KV cache / ephemeral state): in the unlikely event of a region outage, we offer a configurable, customer-approved cross-region replication policy. Replication is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest; keys remain customer-scoped where KMS integration is enabled. Any cross-region replication of ephemeral data requires a pre-authorized policy and generates an automated notification to the primary account owner; our commitment is notification within 2 hours and a full incident summary within 48 hours.
- Operational egress for diagnostics: if a customer enables support-mode debug captures, those captures are stored per the telemetry retention matrix and are exported only to the region specified in the support ticket (customer must approve cross-region transfer if outside the service locus).

4) Audit evidence and attachments
- Attached: 20261105-Service-Locus-Commitment.pdf (formal one-paragraph commitment you can include in procurement) and telemetry-retention-matrix.xlsx (row-level detail per signal type and per deployment model: hosted, dedicated, private).

Exceptions / Notes
- Private (on-prem) deployments: customers operating Redwood Private control all hosting and telemetry retention; Redwood provides the software and opt-in telemetry controls.
- Dedicated: telemetry default retention can be contractually adjusted.

If you need a signed, line-item residency commitment for contract inclusion (e.g., euro-only processing with specified fallback states), we can produce a signed annex and route it through Legal/Contracts (we can have a draft within 48 hours).

Attachments: 20261105-Service-Locus-Commitment.pdf (signed draft), telemetry-retention-matrix.xlsx
